title: After the theatre: malls, Connecticut and recordings
summary: Afterward they played malls and Westchester and Connecticut, and Green made recordings including Mr. Bojangles and On the Amazon.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: And then what happened to the Hustlers? "The Hoofer"
Well, they got a chance to do something with Debut John, Rhythm Red, and on-the-town dancer Raymond
Kailer, and the Godfather went up in some malls for Peter's wife, you see. And we went up into Westchester in different places like that; in Connecticut like that.

And it was during -- I had to make some recordings. I had to make a record for Mr. Paul Winters from Greenpoint, Connecticut. I made "Mr. Bojangles" with Peter, Paul, and Mary Ford. And I had to make another one "On the Amazon" here in Manhattan for Mr. Ed Freeman and his partner, you know. Wherever I was, I mean I had to do the followups.

I say, so and the procedure of our doing these recordings -- we acquired some new youngsters, which was Jonathan Nichols, see. That was our -- Public Tap was our last protege I like to say, because -- and then I had to be a judge one time at a dance contest, and I acquired one.
